question: Does mutational plan synthesis reach OGHarn's +14% median coverage over developer-written harnesses?
answer: NO, on the evidence available. Two C cases were measured on an idle host.

libyaml.result: ZERO viable candidates -- all 8 top-ranked were killed by a smoke test, every one aborting on a valid input
libyaml.why: libyaml is a stateful API guarded by asserts. yaml_parser_set_encoding asserts !parser->encoding; repeating set_input_string or yaml_parser_load re-enters a consumed parser. No header expresses any of it.

brotli.winning_operator: repeat -- the decompress-stream call run twice

VERDICT: The effect on brotli is CONSISTENT IN DIRECTION (5/5) and REAL in the sense that the synthesised candidate is never worse. It is also TINY: +0.34 points, +0.40%, against a target of +14%. At n=5 it does not reach significance (p = 0.056). On libyaml the same operators produce nothing usable at all.
what_this_means_for_the_axis: Mutational synthesis as implemented here does NOT reach OGHarn's result. Two operators -- widen and repeat -- are not enough, and one of them is unsound for stateful APIs. The candidate space widens (x14-x16 valid candidates, reachable surface 8%->52% on jansson) but the extra reach does not convert into coverage at anything like the rate the target requires.
what_is_worth_keeping: The synthesised candidate has a SMALLER spread than the base on brotli, 0.73 against 2.52. A harness that is never worse and varies less is worth something even at +0.4%, and it is a different claim from beating a baseline.
the_honest_limits: Two cases, both C. pugixml and the C++ cases need the cxx_header producer, which probe_synth does not use.
n=5 per case, and p = 0.056 is not significance however consistent the direction looks.
The smoke test admits candidates that survive ONE valid input; a candidate that aborts on the second is still counted viable.
